objects.original: A real-valued C¹ function and its Euclidean gradient, with an affine segment.
objects.reconstructed: A real-valued C¹ function and its Hilbert-space gradient, with the same affine segment.
objects.evidence: The packet module obtains HasGradientAt from hf.differentiable_one; the gradient is the Riesz representative of the actual derivative.

domains.original: All of finite-dimensional real Euclidean space.
domains.reconstructed: All of an arbitrary complete real inner-product space E.
domains.evidence: E has no finite-dimensionality constraint. The declaration specializes to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), but its unrestricted statement is broader.

quantifiers.original: Every x and direction v in the Euclidean domain.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Every x,v in E; every admissible E and C¹ f.
quantifiers.evidence: Changing y to x+v is bijective for fixed x. There is no restriction v≠0. The additional ambient-space generality is recorded in domains.

assumptions.original: Continuous differentiability on the whole Euclidean domain.
assumptions.reconstructed: ContDiff ℝ 1 f on all E; completeness of E.
assumptions.evidence: ContDiff is continuous Fréchet differentiability here. Euclidean completeness is automatic. hc derives scalar continuity and interval integrability; hd derives the segment derivative. Neither is an added source assumption.

conclusion.reconstructed: The same equality, with the intervalIntegral over real Lebesgue measure.
conclusion.evidence: FTC gives the difference of endpoint values. Endpoints have zero Lebesgue mass, so [0,1] and the interval-integral convention agree.

scopes.original: The first FTC identity in the (1.5)→(1.3) proof of part 1.
scopes.reconstructed: One standalone FTC leaf, with no convexity or Hessian conclusion.
scopes.evidence: The publication binding supports monotonicity-to-chord. The lesson consistently describes only this identity and labels the complete inner-product domain.

constant_dependencies.original: Unit integration interval and coefficient one; no modulus in the identity.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same interval and coefficients, independent of dimension or modulus.
constant_dependencies.evidence: No auxiliary constants or parameter restrictions occur in this declaration.

deltas.reconstructed: Arbitrary complete real inner-product whole space
deltas.evidence: Restriction to EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) recovers the source domain. This is not an equivalence claim between the unrestricted source and Lean statements and requires no source repair.
deltas.description: The Lean leaf generalizes the selected finite-dimensional Euclidean source boundary to arbitrary complete real inner-product spaces. The publication lesson explicitly identifies this generalization; acceptance is restricted to the selected Euclidean source boundary, and the unrestricted semantic verdict remains domain-mismatch.

review_evidence: Independently opened the exact primary-source HTML at https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S1.SS2; inspected Definition 1.5, Proposition 1.6 part 1 and its first FTC identity. Audited the supplied current_lean_module and declaration lesson. The chain rule and continuous derivative evaluation justify hd and hc; Mathlib integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt requires precisely the derived derivative and interval integrability. The authored explanation is accurate. Acceptance is for the selected Euclidean FTC source boundary; the complete-inner-product-space extension is explicitly broader and is not a source correction.
